Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which part of an atom has the least mass. The options are electron, nucleus, neutron, and proton. I remember that electrons are really tiny, but I'm not sure how they compare to neutrons and protons. I think protons and neutrons are inside the nucleus, right? 

Wait, I also recall that the mass of a proton is much larger than that of an electron. Let me try to remember the masses. An electron is about 9.11e-31 kg, a proton is around 1.67e-27 kg, and a neutron is about 8.5e-32 kg. So comparing these, the neutron is the smallest. 

But wait, the nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons. So the nucleus mass would be the sum of the protons and neutrons. Since each proton is about 1836 times the mass of an electron, and neutrons are similar, the nucleus must be much more massive than a single neutron. So the neutron itself is lighter than the proton but how does it compare to the nucleus? 

I think the nucleus is way heavier because it's made up of multiple particles. So the neutron, being part of the nucleus, is actually part of a larger structure. But when we're comparing individual particles, the neutron is lighter than the proton. So the least mass would be the neutron. 

Wait, but I'm a bit confused. If the nucleus is made of protons and neutrons, does that mean the nucleus itself has more mass than a single neutron? Yes, because it's made up of multiple neutrons and protons. So the individual neutron is lighter than the proton, but the nucleus is much heavier. So among the options, the neutron has the least mass. 

I think the initial analysis was correct. The neutron has the least mass, so the answer should be C) neutron.
